content.comment_body: [user_name], I've also tested with Gmail, and it's still not working correctly. I've opened a support ticket at [company_name]. It seems we may need to allow a third device to use SMTP... Anyway, I'll update you once I receive more information!

Hello, Ensure the date, time, and all network settings are properly configured. Synchronizing the timestamp is necessary for the SNTP server login. Complete IP configuration is needed for sending requests via the internet to the SNTP server. Hope this is helpful.
Hi, I've synchronized the clock, but it's still not functioning correctly. What do you mean by IP-Setting?
Hello, IP Address, Subnet Mask, and Gateway Address. If these aren't fully configured, then [product_name] won't connect to the email server. Hope this helps.
Have you received a response from [company_name]?

Hello [user_name], Yes, I got some advice from [company_name]. I've tried all the suggestions, but it's still not working. I'm testing with Gmail because it's the simpler approach. [company_name] also requested a CA certificate from the email provider, Gmail in this case, but I don't know how to download it. Do you know how?
This [document] is quite complicated... I was hoping for a direct link to easily download the certificate. Anyway, I'll keep working on resolving this! Thank you!
Maybe this could help? Use Google-managed SSL certificates | Load Balancing | Google Cloud

I'm not sure if this is good news, but I was able to send a test email successfully. Not with Gmail, but with another provider (one.com). I also host a website and email account through one.com. Here's the configuration I used: Server name: SEND.ONE.COM Security: STARTTLS Port: 587 Email: [snip] Password: .......... The test was sent to my personal Gmail account. Surprisingly, I received: "Dear Users: This email is automatically generated by [product_name], please do not reply! If you received this email, the email sending feature works. Here's a multilingual example: English Deutsch Français Русский 简体中文 繁體中文 日本語 한국어... Enjoy using [product_name], [company_name] team More details: [url] IP: 192.168.1.222 Device Name: [product_name]_1" Afterwards, following a breakdown on my machine, I got an alert email. My thoughts: It's disappointing when expectations aren't met. I get promotional messages about new products and imagine all the uses for my machines, but Gmail—the most essential provider—still isn't supported. Using an alternative email server that's possibly less secure works, but Gmail does not. Why does [company_name] release products with incomplete email functionality? I hope my workaround helps others too.
Please avoid posting duplicate questions about the same issue. You already have a dedicated topic for this problem.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing difficulties sending emails from [product_name], particularly with Gmail's SMTP server. Even after syncing clocks and network settings, the email feature remains unreliable. Suggestions from official support, such as acquiring CA certificates, are considered complex. One user managed success with a lesser-known provider, implying that certain servers—mainly Gmail—are problematic. Users express frustration due to the lack of smooth integration with major email services and the perception that the product's email functionality is incomplete.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to offer simple, reliable email sending with popular providers like Gmail, featuring straightforward setup and easy certificate acquisition.
